description: Run identity of the corrected untouched full-history SingleAnchor characterization (Phase D) under the finalized Phase B broker-forced-liquidation model. The run executes the frozen Phase A strategy/account/data values unchanged over the full qualified window and differs from the historical baseline only in the account Stop Out behavior. This file is not a second account contract: every effective strategy parameter, account/ margin value, qualified data identity, session map, run window and missing-data rule remains the immutable frozen baseline contract's; this contract pins that contract and adds the current-model identity and the outcome policy a Phase D classification may accept.
scope: the corrected untouched full-history SingleAnchor characterization (Phase D) only; it does not modify, replace or reinterpret the frozen Phase A baseline contract, its audit register, its run record or its evidence, and it never authorizes a parameter change
canonicalization: The corrected-full-history contract identity is the SHA-256 of this file's UTF-8 text content with CRLF normalized to LF, lower-case hex. It is computed and recorded at launch by run-backtest.ps1 -RunEvidence and re-verified by the corrected-full-history classifier. The file itself is bound to the reviewed source commit and clean tree; no separate register pin exists because the values it references are already pinned by config/baseline-decision-audit.json through the frozen baseline contract hash.

baselineContract.authority: Sole authority for every effective value of the Phase D run: the 30 single-anchor-* parameters (including the full 2019-01-01..2026-06-30 window), the qualified continuous data identity, the session map, the frozen margin/survival contract and the failed-data policy. The corrected run must pass exactly those values; the classifier compares the run's invocation evidence and persisted parameter block against this contract and refuses any divergence. The register pin of this contract hash is checked in addition, so the corrected descriptor cannot silently point at an edited baseline contract.

model.semantics: Reaching the frozen 20% Stop Out condition (or open positions with negative equity) starts deterministic broker-forced liquidation at the executable market side of the triggering quote: the least-profitable open position is force-closed first (equal executable profits tie on the higher immutable trade number), its realized P/L reaches the balance immediately, the surviving inventory is revalued and liquidation continues until the account is restored above the Stop Out condition or no positions remain. A partially liquidated basket continues on its lifetime economics; a fully liquidated basket ends through ExitReason.BrokerLiquidation; an operable account continues processing subsequent historical data. Stop Out is an episode, not a terminal state.
model.changeScope: account Stop Out behavior only, as implemented and independently reviewed in Phase B (Rady70/Lean PR #18, merged 85af343c5fb5105adcdc2a2785600ff436a7f977). No strategy parameter, execution economic, margin value, data or session-map change from the frozen baseline contract is part of the corrected run.
model.terminalFailureKindsNote: A genuine run-ending condition the current implementation itself defines (a strategy invariant failure, a data-quality failure, a session-map coverage failure, an account that cannot be revalued, or a forced close the executor cannot fill) is a preservable Phase D outcome when it is evidenced exactly: the qualified delivered prefix, the recorded failure and the terminal engine-log shape. It is classified, not converted into a completion and not silently retried. AccountStopOut is deliberately absent: it belongs to the historical pre-liquidation model, the current model never raises it, and it can never qualify a Phase D run. A warning that a terminal run looks like an implementation/tooling defect rather than a model outcome is a human interpretation duty recorded with the result; the classifier's duty is to preserve and evidence what happened faithfully.

runHost.parameterChannel: -Parameters (the frozen baseline contract's 30 single-anchor-* values, passed explicitly and unchanged)
runHost.runEvidence: the authoritative run passes -RunEvidence so run-backtest.ps1 writes marketlab-run-invocation.json into the run directory before LEAN is launched (resolved absolute inputs, exact parameter pairs, allow flags, launcher argv, config/algorithm hashes, Git HEAD and dirty state, the qualified runtime binary hashes, the corrected-full-history contract path/hash and the corrected preflight binding) and marketlab-run-outcome.json after the run (LEAN exit code, final helper exit code, the engine-error check and count, the data-monitor result and whether the runtime binaries changed); the corrected-full-history classifier refuses a run directory without either file.
runHost.correctedHistoryContractParameter: -CorrectedHistoryContract MarketLab\config\corrected-full-history-contract.json (with -RunEvidence: the helper and the classifier require this canonical tracked descriptor from the clean reviewed checkout; an arbitrary descriptor path is refused. The descriptor hash is computed and recorded before LEAN launches and the descriptor's frozen-baseline pin is verified against the actual baseline contract hash and the register pin)
runHost.expectedTerminalExceptionParameter: none: under the current model a Stop Out is not terminal, so no launch-time terminal exception is declared. A genuine terminal run failure is classified from the persisted failure record and the one terminal engine ERROR:: line that names the failure exception; any unrelated engine ERROR:: line invalidates the run.
runHost.reviewedCommitParameter: -ReviewedCommit: explicitly approved full 40-character Git SHA, required by build, authoritative preflight and launch; HEAD must equal it and the checkout must be clean
runHost.buildReceiptParameter: -BuildReceipt MarketLab\output\baseline-build.json: successful Build-SingleAnchorBaseline.ps1 rebuild tied to the reviewed source tree, the runtime dependencies and the frozen baseline contract hash; the corrected classifier re-verifies the receipt field by field
runHost.runtimeSelection: dotnet exec --fx-version <receipt runtime version> --roll-forward Disable; the selected .NET 10 framework, dotnet host and hostfxr files are hash-bound

outcomePolicy.completed: The full qualified stream must be delivered (2,332 partitions, 413,750,130 quotes, the qualified first/last quotes and global semantic digest) and verified by the current-model full-stream verifier; the result must name modelRevision 'marketlab-single-anchor-broker-liquidation-v1' and stopOutModel 'BrokerLiquidation'; LEAN exit 0 / helper exit 0 with the engine-error audit performed and zero engine ERROR:: lines; the failed-data requests must classify as the expected source-absent calendar days and the enumerated auxiliary request. Stop Out episodes and forced liquidations inside a completed run are normal research observations, not failures.
outcomePolicy.terminalFailure: A run that ends through one of the current model's own run-ending conditions is preserved exactly and classified: the result carries completed=false and the failure record with its kind, condition, quote and message. The kind and condition must be one exact, case-sensitive reviewed pair (StrategyInvariant/HardBreakevenViolatedByFill, DataQuality/InvalidQuote, DataQuality/OutOfOrderQuote, SessionMap/QuoteOutsideMapCoverage, AccountSurvival/ExecutableMarkUnavailable, BrokerLiquidation/ForcedCloseFailed); any other pair is refused. The faulting quote is bound to the verified historical execution: for accepted-then-faulted kinds (StrategyInvariant, AccountSurvival, BrokerLiquidation) it must equal the final processed quote (and therefore the delivered last quote), while for pre-acceptance kinds (DataQuality, SessionMap) the refused quote must equal the next qualified source quote after the verified delivered prefix; the complete failure quote is persisted in the classification evidence. Delivery must be the exact qualified prefix ending at the last processed quote (the partial terminal day verified against the native ZIP prefix); the outcome must show LEAN exit 1 / helper exit 1 with the engine-error audit performed, exactly one terminal engine ERROR:: line (the SetRuntimeError line naming the failure's exception type) that matches the recorded failure, and no unrelated engine ERROR:: lines. The failed-data requests are classified with the request horizon as their bound: the last processed day for accepted-then-faulted kinds and the verified faulting quote's day for pre-acceptance kinds (the feed had to advance through the intervening calendar days); an actual failed request for a source-absent day after that horizon is invalid, not an expected absence. The terminal prefix's global delivered semantic digest is recorded but not independently recomputed (the per-partition digests and the native terminal-day ZIP prefix are the verified identity; deliveryVerification.globalSemanticDigestVerified is false for a terminal prefix and true for the completed full stream). The failure kind, condition, quote and message are reported as the run outcome.
outcomePolicy.invalid: Any other ending, a missing or mismatched evidence record, a terminal kind/condition pair outside the exact reviewed set, a faulting quote that does not match the engine's processed/pre-acceptance semantics, an engine ERROR:: line beyond the single recorded-failure line, a failed request for a source-absent day after the request horizon, a changed runtime binary, a dirty working tree at launch, a delivered stream that is neither the full qualified population nor the exact qualified prefix, or a Stop Out episode that is described as a failure or a completion that hides one: the run cannot be certified as Phase D evidence.
outcomePolicy.stopOutIsNotTerminal: Under the current model the 20% Stop Out condition invokes broker liquidation and processing continues whenever the account remains operable. A Phase D completion may contain any number of Stop Out episodes, forced liquidations and fully liquidated baskets; none of them makes the run terminal and none may be withheld from the characterization.

steps: Independently review the exact final PR head of the corrected-full-history support revision. Under the current project rule (Windows-only local validation; no hosted CI before merge), do not dispatch .github/workflows/marketlab-final-validation.yml on the unmerged PR head: that workflow remains an optional, separately authorized hosted confirmation and is not part of the Phase D finalization. After the exact-head review approves the candidate, merge/finalize (the support author does not merge) and synchronize local master; verify the merged master tree is the reviewed tree, then set $ReviewedCommit to the resulting merged master SHA: Build-SingleAnchorBaseline.ps1 and Assert-BaselineBuild require a clean checkout whose HEAD equals $ReviewedCommit, so the Phase D build and run use the merged master source, not the pre-merge PR-head SHA. Build: pwsh -File MarketLab\scripts\Build-SingleAnchorBaseline.ps1 -ReviewedCommit $ReviewedCommit. Stop on any nonzero exit.
Report the frozen contract identity: pwsh -File MarketLab\scripts\Get-SingleAnchorBaselineInvocation.ps1 -ReviewedCommit $ReviewedCommit. The corrected run consumes the same frozen parameter values.

Corrected preflight: pwsh -File MarketLab\scripts\Test-SingleAnchorCorrectedFullHistory.ps1 -Preflight -Contract MarketLab\config\corrected-full-history-contract.json -ReviewedCommit $ReviewedCommit -BuildReceipt MarketLab\output\baseline-build.json -OutputPath MarketLab\output\corrected-history-preflight.json. Stop on any nonzero exit. This verifies the corrected descriptor, its frozen-baseline pin and register pin, the clean reviewed checkout, the source-bound build receipt and the complete qualified tree without replaying history.

Only after separate authorization to run Phase D, invoke the exact rendered helper command. It repeats the corrected preflight immediately before launch, compares the actual arguments with the frozen contract, pins the runtime and saves build/preflight evidence. Do not pass -AllowEngineErrors and do not pass -ExpectedTerminalException.

Classify the result: pwsh -File MarketLab\scripts\Test-SingleAnchorCorrectedFullHistory.ps1 -Contract MarketLab\config\corrected-full-history-contract.json -RunDirectory <run directory> -ReviewedCommit $ReviewedCommit. A completed run must reproduce the qualified full stream and name the current model; a terminal run must prove the delivered prefix and the recorded failure. The classifier also reconciles every failed data request with the monitor.

Retain the build receipt, corrected preflight, invocation evidence, outcome evidence, classification, effective parameter block and source/session/delivery provenance with the run. The corrected full-history run has not been executed by this support change.
runProcedure.exactRunCommand: pwsh -File MarketLab\scripts\run-backtest.ps1 -Configuration Release -Config MarketLab/config/backtesting.json -AlgorithmTypeName SingleAnchorVNextAlgorithm -AlgorithmLanguage CSharp -AlgorithmLocation MarketLab\src\SingleAnchor\bin\Release\MarketLab.SingleAnchor.dll -DataFolder E:\MarketLab\data\lean\xauusd-dukascopy -Parameters "single-anchor-symbol:XAUUSD,single-anchor-market:dukascopy,single-anchor-security-type:Cfd,single-anchor-start-date:2019-01-01,single-anchor-end-date:2026-06-30,single-anchor-cash:20000,single-anchor-session-map:marketlab-sessions/xauusd-sessions.json,single-anchor-step-percent:0.25,single-anchor-base-lot:0.10,single-anchor-normal-trade-count:4,single-anchor-hard-be-ceiling-percent:4.478,single-anchor-escape-enabled:true,single-anchor-escape-profit-units:0.05,single-anchor-escape-minimum-open-positions:2,single-anchor-fixed-tp-units:0,single-anchor-trailing-enabled:true,single-anchor-trailing-activation-units:0.50,single-anchor-trailing-drop-units:0.25,single-anchor-commission-buffer:0,single-anchor-point-value-per-lot:100,single-anchor-volume-step:0.01,single-anchor-minimum-volume:0.01,single-anchor-maximum-volume:50,single-anchor-commission-per-lot:0,single-anchor-slippage:0,single-anchor-projected-spread:0.50,single-anchor-buy-swap-per-lot-per-day:0,single-anchor-sell-swap-per-lot-per-day:0,single-anchor-research-account:true,single-anchor-margin-enabled:true" -AllowMissingData -RunEvidence -CorrectedHistoryContract MarketLab\config\corrected-full-history-contract.json -ReviewedCommit $ReviewedCommit -BuildReceipt MarketLab\output\baseline-build.json
runProcedure.runEvidenceRequirements: The run must use the reviewed and merged corrected-full-history support revision with a successful source-bound build receipt. Persist baseline-build.json, corrected-history-preflight.json, the pre-run invocation evidence, the post-run outcome evidence and the corrected-full-history classification. Bind the tracked replay record SHA-256 to the local record, composition manifest, all 2,332 partition ZIP hashes and auxiliary files. Persist the effective parameters and UTC window, runtime version/directory, full or terminal-prefix delivery counts/digests, the final processed quote, the research account/margin state and every Stop Out episode/forced liquidation. Compare all dependencies before and after execution.
runProcedure.notYetRun: The corrected untouched full-history run has not been executed. This descriptor and the support scripts that consume it are prepared for independent review first; executing Phase D requires separate explicit authorization and the reviewed revision as the run source.

relationshipToPhaseARecord.phaseA: The first untouched full-history baseline (Phase A, run 2026-09-28) remains the historical record of the pre-broker-liquidation Stop Out model: reaching Stop Out terminated the run at 2020-03-23T12:06:26.292Z with basket #276 open and 36 positions. That record, its contract and its evidence are unchanged and must never be rewritten to claim broker liquidation.
relationshipToPhaseARecord.phaseB: Phase B implemented deterministic broker-forced liquidation (merged through Rady70/Lean PR #18); Phase C qualified it locally over the bounded March 2020 region. This contract and the corrected-full-history classifier are the Phase D support prepared by the support change that introduces this file.
relationshipToPhaseARecord.phaseD: A Phase D result is a new, separately identified current-model characterization. It may contain Stop Out episodes and forced liquidations that the Phase A record could not contain, and it reports the post-liquidation continuation the Phase A record deliberately did not simulate. It is never merged into or compared as a competing number with the Phase A trigger state.
